newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Great Witnesses" to speak on Mitterrand in Paris.
newsitem.headline: "Great Witnesses" to speak on Mitterrand in Paris.

text.p: UNESCO said on Tuesday many foreign leaders and major figures of the 1980 and 1990s would appear as "Great Witnesses" of the late French president Francois Mitterrand's international policy at a Paris seminar next month.

Cuban President Fidel Castro was among international figures expected at the January 9-10 seminar called "Francois Mitterrand - Peace and Development - Testimonies" and marking the first anniversary of Mitterrand's death.

Former European Commission president Jacques Delors, Haiti's ex-president Jean-Bertrand Aristide and former foreign ministers Hans Dietrich Genscher of Germany and David Owen of Britain were also scheduled to attend.

Former U.S. and Soviet presidents George Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, ex-Iraeli premier Shimon Peres and South African President Nelson Mandela have been invited, UNESCO said.

The seminar, at the Paris headquarters of UNESCO (United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation), intends to study Socialist Mitterrand's influence on international relations and little-known aspects of his 1981-95 presidency.
